title: SOMA lets Claude Code or Codex design printable 3D parts as CadQuery code
summary: Makers who need a case or bracket often don't want to learn CAD. SOMA lets a CLI coding agent write the part as CadQuery code. The app builds and shows each version, and the user points at problems until the part fits, then exports it for printing.
agent_role: The agent writes and edits the Python model code and runs build, analyze and render commands. It also produces drawings and animations. The human describes the part, inspects it, measures it and marks fixes.
outcome: The author reports mostly testing with Claude Code and Claude Opus 5.5, with very good results. It is an early 0.8.0 prototype.
what_they_did: A developer built a desktop app around any CLI coding agent, such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode or Gemini CLI. The agent gets a soma command-line tool and an AGENTS.md with project rules. The user describes a part, for example a Raspberry Pi 5 case with lid vents in PETG. The agent writes CadQuery code that SOMA rebuilds on every change. The user clicks, measures or sketches on the view to request fixes, then exports STL or 3MF.
how_it_went: The author says it was mostly tested with Claude Code and Opus 5.5, with very good results. It is labelled an early prototype, and the app itself was largely written by coding agents.
worth_knowing: The install is over 1 GB and the packages are unsigned. It is mainly tested on Windows. You bring your own agent subscription.
prompt: Design a parametric 3D part in CadQuery: [describe the part, e.g. a case for a [device] with vents], to be printed in [material] on [printer]. Make key dimensions adjustable parameters. Build the model, check wall thickness and overhangs, and render a preview. Summarise the dimensions and any printability concerns. Wait for my feedback before exporting to STL.

curation.rationale: An original maker workflow: a CLI coding agent writes CadQuery models while the app builds, renders and analyses them for feedback. Code and a concrete loop are available, but there are no documented project outcomes beyond the author's 'very good results'.
